m.title: CPU Performance and Embedded Systems
m.q: Compare CPU A: 2 GHz, two cores with CPU B: 3 GHz, four cores, with other factors unspecified.
st: B has more cycles per second.
B also has more cores for potentially parallel work.
It may perform better in suitable tasks, but other hardware/software factors matter.
Do not state that it must always run every program faster.

wSteps: It performs a specific function rather than general-purpose computing.

k.code:
clockA = 2
clockB = 3
if clockB > clockA then
    print("B has higher clock speed")
endif
p: Explain your predicted result using the first assignment or test.
Add a separate equality test to report when the two clock speeds match.
k.a: At 3 GHz versus 2 GHz it prints B has higher clock speed. After setting clockB to 1 there is no output because the condition is false. A test clockB == clockA can report equality. Clock speed alone cannot establish which CPU runs every workload faster.

e: State two CPU factors affecting performance. [2 marks]
Clock speed, cache size, number of cores (any two).
Explain why a larger cache may improve performance. [3 marks]
Frequently needed instructions/data can be accessed faster, reducing waiting for RAM.
Give an example of an embedded system and explain why it qualifies. [3 marks]
For example a washing-machine controller: built into the device for a dedicated control task.
v: The number of CPU cycles per second, commonly measured in GHz.

x: More CPU cores can improve performance for tasks that run in parallel.
r: State the purpose of MAR and MDR.
MAR: address of memory location accessed; MDR: data/instruction being transferred.
Give a suitable boundary value when valid ages are 13–18.
13 or 18, plus an adjacent invalid such as 12 or 19 for a test set.
Explain why a 2D array needs two indexes.
One selects the row; the other selects the column.
Explain why testing after debugging is necessary.
To verify the correction and ensure no new faults were introduced.

mastery.task: Design a comparison tool that reads clock speed, core count and cache size for two CPUs, then explains why declaring a single 'winner' is not justified by clock speed alone.
mastery.hint: A single IF tests only one factor; multiple factors can trade off.
mastery.answer: Model: compare each specification separately, output differences, and state that workload and architecture affect actual performance. Tests: one CPU has higher clock but fewer cores; equal clock; same cores with different cache.
